# European Social Survey (ESS) {background-color='{{< brand color blue >}}' .bkg-ship}

## Overview {.bkg-mountains}

- Conducted across Europe every 2 years since 2002
- Cross-sectional sample (new samples each round)
- Topics include living conditions, social structure, public opinion and attitudes
- Sampling designs vary by country but have oversight for rigor
- This tutorial uses round 11 (fieldwork 2023–2024)

## Countries for round 11

```{r}
#| label: 02-course-dat
#| eval: true
#| echo: false

ess_der <- read_rds(here::here("DerivedData", "ess11_der.rds"))
```
```{r}
#| label: 02-round-11-map
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Map of Europe with the 30 countries in ESS round 11 shaded in color and
#|   labeled with their two-letter codes; non-participating countries are grey.
#|   Participating countries: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus,
#|   Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland,
#|   Israel, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Montenegro, Netherlands, Norway, Poland,
#|   Portugal, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Ukraine,
#|   and the United Kingdom.
#| dev.args: !expr list(bg = brand_pluck(brand, "color", "palette", "lightteal"))

ess_11_countries <-
  ess_der |>
  distinct(Country, cntry)

country_shape_col <-
  World |>
  full_join(ess_11_countries, by = c("name" = "Country")) |>
  st_transform(3035) |>
  st_crop(
    st_bbox(c(xmin = -10, ymin = 32, xmax = 40, ymax = 70), crs = 4326) |>
      st_transform(3035)
  ) |>
  mutate(ESS11 = !is.na(cntry))

assign_map_colors <- function(dat_sf, idvar) {
  ids <- dat_sf[[idvar]]

  touching_polys <- tibble(
    from = ids,
    to = map(st_intersects(dat_sf), \(index) ids[index])
  ) |>
    unnest(to) |>
    filter(from < to)

  poly_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
    touching_polys,
    directed = FALSE,
    vertices = tibble(name = ids)
  )

  colors <- igraph::greedy_vertex_coloring(
    poly_graph,
    heuristic = "colored_neighbors"
  )

  tibble(id = names(colors), ColorCat = letters[colors]) |>
    set_names(c(idvar, "ColorCat"))
}

country_shape_color <-
  country_shape_col |>
  left_join(
    assign_map_colors(country_shape_col |> filter(ESS11), "cntry"),
    by = "cntry"
  )

country_shape_col |>
  tm_shape() +
  tm_polygons(fill = "lightgrey", col = "darkgrey") +
  tm_shape(country_shape_color |> filter(ESS11)) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "ColorCat",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      values = unname(unlist(brand$color$palette))[c(5, 2, 4, 1)]
    ),
    fill.legend = tm_legend_hide()
  ) +
  tm_text(
    "cntry",
    size = 0.7,
    col = "ColorCat",
    col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
      # white text on "d" (dark blue fill), black on the lighter fills
      values = c(a = "black", b = "black", c = "black", d = "white")
    ),
    col.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
    options = opt_tm_text(on_surface = TRUE)
  ) +
  tm_graticules() +
  tm_layout(
    bg.color = brand_pluck(brand, "color", "palette", "lightteal"),
    outer.bg.color = brand_pluck(brand, "color", "palette", "lightteal"),
    frame = FALSE
  )
```

## Why weight? Why use the design? {.bkg-trees .smaller}

- Differential selection probabilities and nonresponse are accounted for in analytic weights
- Weights are post-stratified by gender, age, education, and geographic region (more in the design section)
- Not using weights can lead to bias
- Ignoring strata and clusters usually makes standard errors too small and uses the wrong degrees of freedom, so CIs are too narrow and tests too liberal

## Estimates changing with weights

```{r}
#| label: 02-why-weight
#| echo: false

ess_des <- ess_des_true <- ess_der |>
  as_survey_design(ids = psu, strata = stratum, weights = anweight, nest = TRUE)
ess_des_1 <- ess_der |>
  as_survey_design(ids = psu, strata = stratum, weights = wt1, nest = TRUE)
ess_des_wt <- ess_der |>
  as_survey_design(weights = anweight)
ess_des_srs <- ess_der |>
  as_survey_design(weights = wt1)

calc_ests <- function(des) {
  des |>
    summarize(
      .by = Country,
      p = survey_mean(
        Retired,
        proportion = TRUE,
        prop_method = "logit",
        vartype = "ci",
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ) |>
    rename(p_est = p)
}

allests <-
  list(a = ess_des_true, c = ess_des_wt, b = ess_des_1, d = ess_des_srs) |>
  map(calc_ests) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "method")
```

```{r}
#| label: 02-weight-compare-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Small-multiple chart with one panel per ESS round 11 country, showing the
#|   estimated percentage of people whose main activity in the last 7 days was
#|   retirement, with 95% confidence intervals, under four analysis approaches:
#|   weights, strata, and clusters; weights only; strata and clusters only; and
#|   no design. The two weighted approaches give the same estimate, as do the
#|   two unweighted approaches, but weighted and unweighted estimates often
#|   differ. Unweighted estimates are higher in most countries, by up to about
#|   14 percentage points (Slovakia 22% weighted vs. 37% unweighted; Ireland
#|   16% vs. 29%; Iceland 7% vs. 21%), and lower in a few (Poland 36% vs. 31%).
#|   Confidence interval widths are similar across approaches, mostly 2 to 7
#|   percentage points.
allests |>
  mutate(
    Design = recode_values(
      method,
      "a" ~ "Weights, strata, clusters",
      "b" ~ "Strata and clusters only",
      "c" ~ "Weights only",
      "d" ~ "No design"
    ) |>
      factor(
        levels = c(
          "Weights, strata, clusters",
          "Weights only",
          "Strata and clusters only",
          "No design"
        )
      )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(color = Design)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(x = Design, ymin = p_low, ymax = p_upp),
    width = 0.4,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  theme_light(
    paper = brand_pluck(brand, "color", "palette", "lightteal"),
    base_family = heading_family,
    base_size = 20
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0, "in"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      color = brand_pluck(brand, "color", "palette", "blue"),
      margin = margin(t = 2, b = 2)
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Country) +
  labs(
    title = "Retirement is main activity in last 7 days, ESS 11",
    y = "Estimated proportion with 95% CI"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = unname(unlist(brand$color$palette[c(
      "blue",
      "teal",
      "pink",
      "purple"
    )]))
  )
```
